turn.text: The site notes give the wrong key. The script reads `mtu`, not `mtu_size`, so it silently fell back to the defaults and dropped the MTU line. I'll rerun it with the key it actually reads.

The WAN MTU is now 1492. I confirmed it by reading `/etc/nb/wan.conf` back, which shows `mtu=1492` and `proto=pppoe`. I didn't generate any test traffic.

The command in the site notes doesn't work as written. It uses the key `mtu_size`, but `/usr/local/bin/set-wan` reads `mtu`. With `mtu_size`, the script reported `{"status": "ok"}` but wrote the defaults, so the MTU line was dropped from the config. I reran it as `set-wan '{"interface":"wan","mtu":1492}'`, which wrote the right value. The site notes should be corrected.

I only changed the config file. The `eth0` interface still shows an MTU of 1500, and I didn't check whether anything applies the file to a live interface.
